bear_case: The 10Y rising 6 bps to 4.48% on a day when S&P 500 futures are up only 0.46% is the first signal the post-Iran deal bond rally is exhausting — the 30Y (estimated ~4.91%) has narrowed its buffer to the 5.00% regime trigger from 15 bps to fewer than 10 bps, meaning a single Warsh sentence or a weak 30Y auction could re-breach the regime threshold before the close on June 17. Goldman Sachs has scrapped all 2026 rate cut forecasts and doubled its estimated odds of modest hikes to 20%; a Reuters poll of 102 economists shows 72 expecting no change through year-end — the 70% CME FedWatch probability of a year-end hike is consensus, not a tail scenario. When the dot plot drops at 2:30 PM ET June 17, if the 2026 median shows zero cuts or the 2027 median is above 3.75%, equities at 22.7x forward P/E face a multiple compression of 5–8% regardless of oil disinflation — NVDA's $85B in bond orders cannot offset a structural re-rating of the discount rate. The formal Iran signing takes place on Juneteenth (June 19, market closed), meaning the first real-time market reaction to implementation developments — including potential mine-clearance complications in the Strait — would be Monday June 20, creating a two-day information gap. **If the dot plot shows no 2026 cuts AND the 30Y rises above 5.00% within 24 hours of the June 17 Warsh presser, BUY reverts to HOLD immediately — do not wait for a weekly close. Conversely, if SPX closes above 7,460 today for the second consecutive session AND Warsh June 17 delivers neutral language, BUY upgrades to HIGH conviction and TBT reduces by 50%.**
